generated_ideas.Abstract: As artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI, continues to reshape labor markets, traditional AI safety frameworks prioritize existential and technical risks while overlooking critical human-centric challenges. Risk Factors and Limitations: Potential resistance from major AI firms to adopt pro-worker policies.
Challenges in designing and implementing collective licensing frameworks across different jurisdictions.
The complexity of accurately measuring the long-term impacts of proposed interventions on labor markets.

firms. By proposing actionable interventions such as collective licensing for 
AI-generated content, mandatory AI watermarking, and robust retraining policies,
we aim to enhance the resilience of labor markets. This paper calls for an 
inclusive dialogue among stakeholders, emphasizing the need for policies that 
not only safeguard against the adverse effects of AI but also promote shared 
prosperity. Our framework aims to establish a sustainable relationship between 
AI and labor that empowers workers and fosters equitable growth.

Current AI safety discussions neglect the systemic risks posed by generative AI 
on labor markets, necessitating a shift towards pro-worker governance frameworks
that prioritize economic justice.

labor markets, traditional AI safety frameworks prioritize existential and

not only safeguard against the adverse effects of AI but also promote shared 
prosperity. Our framework aims to establish a sustainable relationship between 
AI and labor that empowers workers and fosters equitable growth.

Abstract:
As artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI, continues to reshape 
labor markets, traditional AI safety frameworks prioritize existential and 
technical risks while overlooking critical human-centric challenges. This 
position paper advocates for a paradigm shift towards a pro-worker governance 
framework that addresses the systemic risks posed by AI on economic justice and 
labor rights. We identify six key risks, including the exacerbation of technical
debt, disproportionate job displacement, and the monopolistic tendencies of AI 
firms. By proposing actionable interventions such as collective licensing for 
AI-generated content, mandatory AI watermarking, and robust retraining policies,
we aim to enhance the resilience of labor markets. This paper calls for an 
inclusive dialogue among stakeholders, emphasizing the need for policies that 
not only safeguard against the adverse effects of AI but also promote shared 
prosperity. Our framework aims to establish a sustainable relationship between 
AI and labor that empowers workers and fosters equitable growth.

Your research idea:


Title:
Reimagining AI Safety: A Pro-Worker Framework for the Future of Work
Abstract:
As artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI, continues to reshape 
labor markets, traditional AI safety frameworks prioritize existential and 
technical risks while overlooking critical human-centric challenges. This 
position paper advocates for a paradigm shift towards a pro-worker governance 
framework that addresses the systemic risks posed by AI on economic justice and 
labor rights. We identify six key risks, including the exacerbation of technical
debt, disproportionate job displacement, and the monopolistic tendencies of AI 
firms. By proposing actionable interventions such as collective licensing for 
AI-generated content, mandatory AI watermarking, and robust retraining policies,
we aim to enhance the resilience of labor markets. This paper calls for an 
inclusive dialogue among stakeholders, emphasizing the need for policies that 
not only safeguard against the adverse effects of AI but also promote shared 
prosperity. Our framework aims to establish a sustainable relationship between 
AI and labor that empowers workers and fosters equitable growth.
Short Hypothesis:
Current AI safety discussions neglect the systemic risks posed by generative AI 
on labor markets, necessitating a shift towards pro-worker governance frameworks
that prioritize economic justice.
Experiment Plan: Conduct a series of surveys and interviews with workers and 
industry leaders to assess perceptions of generative AI's impact on job security
and skills.
Simulate labor market scenarios using agent-based modeling to evaluate the 
effects of proposed interventions (e.g., collective licensing, retraining 
programs) on job displacement and economic outcomes.
Test the effectiveness of AI watermarking techniques in reducing the prevalence 
of low-quality AI-generated content and its impact on creative labor markets.

Title:
Reimagining AI Safety: A Pro-Worker Framework for the Future of Work
Abstract:
As artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI, continues to reshape 
labor markets, traditional AI safety frameworks prioritize existential and 
technical risks while overlooking critical human-centric challenges. This 
position paper advocates for a paradigm shift towards a pro-worker governance 
framework that addresses the systemic risks posed by AI on economic justice and 
labor rights. We identify six key risks, including the exacerbation of technical
debt, disproportionate job displacement, and the monopolistic tendencies of AI 
firms. By proposing actionable interventions such as collective licensing for 
AI-generated content, mandatory AI watermarking, and robust retraining policies,
we aim to enhance the resilience of labor markets. This paper calls for an 
inclusive dialogue among stakeholders, emphasizing the need for policies that 
not only safeguard against the adverse effects of AI but also promote shared 
prosperity. Our framework aims to establish a sustainable relationship between 
AI and labor that empowers workers and fosters equitable growth.
Short Hypothesis:
Current AI safety discussions neglect the systemic risks posed by generative AI 
on labor markets, necessitating a shift towards pro-worker governance frameworks
that prioritize economic justice.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Potential resistance from major AI firms to adopt 
pro-worker policies.
Challenges in designing and implementing collective licensing frameworks across 
different jurisdictions.
The complexity of accurately measuring the long-term impacts of proposed 
interventions on labor markets.

).item()


# Function to extract and print metrics
def print_metrics(experiment_data):
    for activation_name, activation_data in experiment_data[
        "activation_function_comparison"
    ].items():
        print(f"Metrics for Activation Function: {activation_name}")

        for batch_size, batch_data in 
activation_data["batch_size_tuning"].items():
            train_losses = batch_data["losses"]["train"]
            val_losses = batch_data["losses"]["val"]
            PWIS_metrics = batch_data["metrics"]["val"]

            best_train_loss = min(train_losses) if train_losses else None
            best_val_loss = min(val_losses) if val_losses else None
            best_PWIS = max(PWIS_metrics) if PWIS_metrics else None

            print(f"  Batch Size: {batch_size}")
            print(
                f"    Best Training Loss: {best_train_loss:.4f}"
                if best_train_loss is not None
                else "    Best Training Loss: N/A"
            )
            print(
                f"    Best Validation Loss: {best_val_loss:.4f}"
                if best_val_loss is not None
                else "    Best Validation Loss: N/A"
            )
            print(
                f"    Best PWIS: {best_PWIS:.4f}"
                if best_PWIS is not None
                else "    Best PWIS: N/A"
            )


print_metrics(experiment_data)

As artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI, continues to reshape 
labor markets, traditional AI safety frameworks prioritize existential and 
technical risks while overlooking critical human-centric challenges. This 
position paper advocates for a paradigm shift towards a pro-worker governance 
framework that addresses the systemic risks posed by AI on economic justice and 
labor rights. We identify six key risks, including the exacerbation of technical
debt, disproportionate job displacement, and the monopolistic tendencies of AI 
firms. By proposing actionable interventions such as collective licensing for 
AI-generated content, mandatory AI watermarking, and robust retraining policies,
we aim to enhance the resilience of labor markets. This paper calls for an 
inclusive dialogue among stakeholders, emphasizing the need for policies that 
not only safeguard against the adverse effects of AI but also promote shared 
prosperity. Our framework aims to establish a sustainable relationship between 
AI and labor that empowers workers and fosters equitable growth.

that prioritize economic justice.

Challenges in designing and implementing collective licensing frameworks across 
different jurisdictions.

interventions on labor markets.
